b.answer:
Worked example: a Harvest Lane test scenario. Search Rows returns 3 test orders → HTTP POST to a webhook.site URL set to return 500. Storing of incomplete executions is switched on for the Break run.

RunHandler on HTTPRun statusHTTP bubbleWhat happened to the bundles
1IgnoreSuccess3 errors, all skippedEach failed bundle was dropped; the run carried on and ended normally
2Resume (substitute: booking_id = "none")Success3 bundles outAll three continued with the substitute output, as if the call worked
3Break (no auto-retry)Warningfailed bundles storedEach failure was saved in Incomplete executions to finish later; note in your table whether later bundles were still processed
4CommitSuccess1 errorThe run stopped at the first failure; bundles 2 and 3 were never processed; any work already done was kept

Compared with Card 2: Ignore = skip, Success ✓. Resume = substitute and continue, Success ✓. Break = incomplete execution, Warning ✓. Commit = stop, keep what's done, skip the rest, Success ✓.

Log line: "Four directives tested against a 500; statuses match the directive table."
mistakes: Running Break with storing of incomplete executions switched off, then recording "nothing happened".
Recording only the run status and not what happened to bundles 2 and 3.
Using a webhook.site URL that returns 200, so no handler ever fires.
Mixing up Commit and Ignore: Commit stops the run, Ignore skips one bundle and carries on.
b.pass: A four-row table (Ignore, Resume, Break, Commit) gives each run's status and what happened to the remaining bundles, and it matches Card 2: Success, Success, Warning, Success.
b.redo: Send it back if a directive is missing, if a status doesn't match the run history, or if the table was copied from the card rather than observed.

s.answer:
Worked example: Harvest Lane's 8 p.m. run, hardened, with three test orders (HL-T1, HL-T2, HL-T3) and the courier faked on webhook.site.

ModuleHandler
HTTP · Weather (Open-Meteo)Resume: rain_chance = "unknown"
HTTP · Book courierGmail alert to Tolu (error type, message, order, area) → Break: 3 attempts, 15 minutes apart
Message customerAdd a Row to Errors (time, scenario, module, order_id, message) → Ignore
Sheets · Add to DeliveriesBreak, 2 retries

Scenario settings: storing of incomplete executions on; email notifications for errors and warnings on.

TestWhat I didWhat happenedOrders lost
Courier down, then upwebhook.site returns 503; Run once; at 20:10 switched it to 2013 alert emails; run status Warning; 3 incomplete executions; at the 20:15 retry all 3 completed and bookings appeared0
Weather downWeather URL pointed at a webhook.site address returning 500Run succeeded; rider messages read "Rain chance: unknown"0
Invalid phoneHL-T2 phone set to 0803One Errors row for HL-T2; HL-T1 and HL-T3 messaged0 (HL-T2 flagged for a call)

Sample alert: Subject "Courier booking failed · HL-T1". Body: "connection error: 503 Service Unavailable. Order HL-T1 for Test Customer, Bodija. Make will retry automatically."

Submit: the handler plan, the test table, screenshots of the incomplete executions before and after recovery, one alert email and the Errors row.
mistakes: Putting Ignore on the courier booking, so failed bookings silently disappear.
Retrying a 401 or 400, which can never succeed and burns credits.
Resuming with a risky default (such as a blank booking) instead of a harmless one like "unknown".
Testing only the happy path, never switching webhook.site to 503 and back.
s.pass: Three tests are shown (courier down then up, weather down, invalid phone) with zero lost orders, an alert or Errors row for every failure, and incomplete executions that completed on their own after the courier came back.
s.redo: Send it back if any test is missing, if bookings had to be completed by hand, or if a failure left no alert and no log.

g.answer:
Worked example: Harvest Lane's shared Errors tab (scenario, module, type, message, time) and a Monday 08:00 report scenario.

#ModuleSettings
1Sheets · Search RowsErrors where time ≥ formatDate(addDays(now; -7); "YYYY-MM-DD")
2Numeric aggregatorCOUNT · Group by: {{1.scenario}} | {{1.type}} · Source: module 1
3Array aggregatorCollects key and count; then get(sort(3.array; "desc"; "count"); 1) gives the top problem
4Text aggregatorOne line per group, source: module 2
5GmailTo Tolu: report below

Suggested fix, chosen by error type:

switch(lower(top.type);
  "connection"; "Provider outage: retries are in place; ask them for maintenance times.";
  "data";       "Bad input: add sheet validation or a filter before the call.";
  "rate-limit"; "Too many calls: spread the schedule or add a pause.";
  "Open the run in History and fix the mapping.")

Sample report (simulated week):

Scenario | typeErrors
HL · 8 p.m. run | connection (courier 503)9
HL · Customer messages | data (invalid phone)6
HL · Payments | data (missing metadata.order_id)4
HL · Invoice intake | connection (AI timeout)2
Total21

Top problem: 8 p.m. run, courier 503 (9). All recovered on retry; no orders lost.
Suggested fix: Provider outage: retries are in place; ask the courier for maintenance times.

Check: a COUNTIFS on the Errors tab for the same week gives the same four numbers.

Submit: the Errors tab (simulated rows are fine), the report scenario screenshot, the email and the COUNTIFS check.
mistakes: Only some scenarios write to the shared Errors tab, so the report undercounts.
Grouping by scenario only, so different problems in one scenario are lumped together.
Forgetting the 7-day date filter, so every week's report includes all past errors.
A "suggested fix" that is generic for every error type instead of matched to the top one.
g.pass: A week of real or simulated errors produces one email that counts errors by scenario and type correctly (matching a manual count), names the top problem, and gives a suggested fix that fits it.
g.redo: Send it back if counts don't match the Errors tab, if the top problem is wrong, or if the report isn't readable without opening Make.
